reference.title: Power Sled Push
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Short, rhythmic breaths with the steps; keep the brace.

prescription.load: Sled load is user-chosen: heavy enough that every step is a hard drive, light enough to keep moving without stalling.
prescription.progression: Add load or distance when every set stays fast and smooth.

cues.text: Hands on the sled poles at about chest height, arms long, body leaning well forward so the shoulders are ahead of the hips.
Drive the sled forward with short, powerful steps, pushing the floor back through the balls of the feet; keep the lean and a flat back.
Stop with the feet together and the body still leaning into the poles.

mistakes.mistake: Standing up tall behind the sled
mistakes.fix: Lean in so the push goes forward through the arms, not down into the sled.
Short, quick steps keep the sled moving.
Brace and keep a long spine from head to hips.

kinematics.norm: Short steps under or just ahead of the hips (common coaching)
Quick, about 1.5-2 steps per second (common coaching)
Forward lean of about 30-50 degrees with the arms long (common coaching)
The sled slides on its runners, moved by the hands on the poles (machine design)
kinematics.setup: Hands 100.7 cm high, 50 cm ahead of the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Sled travels 94.5 cm; hands within 0.19 cm of the handle line

sources.title: GymVisual, Power Sled Push, video (movement reference)

cautions: Clear the path and use a surface the sled slides on evenly.
Keep the head in line with the back; do not look down between the arms.
Start with a light sled to learn the steps.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: lighter load and shorter steps.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Support the bent stance knee under the load (the knee stays more bent than in normal walking, Winwood 2014).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Support the bent stance knee under the load (the knee stays more bent than in normal walking, Winwood 2014).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives each step and keeps the hips extended.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drives each step and keeps the hips extended.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Push off at the end of each step.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push off at the end of each step.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Hold the arms forward against the poles.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Hold the arms forward against the poles.
muscleNotes.core: Carrying produced more trunk muscle activity than holding the same dumbbells still (Int J Exerc Sci 2024).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk tall (Int J Exerc Sci 2024: longissimus and multifidus more active while carrying).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk tall (Int J Exerc Sci 2024: longissimus and multifidus more active while carrying).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades on the ribs while pressing.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades on the ribs while pressing.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the heavy handles the whole set; grip is usually what fails first.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the heavy handles the whole set; grip is usually what fails first.
